Introduction
This document provides essential information on the components of the Product Safety & Quality Key
Issue to enable users of ESG Ratings to understand how MSCI Sustainability & Climate ("MSCI") outputs
are determined. Product Safety & Quality is a Key Issue in the Social Pillar of the MSCI ESG Ratings
model. Companies are evaluated on their exposure to possible recalls or product safety concerns, the
strength of their supply chain and sourcing systems, their quality management efforts in manufacturing
and their responsible marketing practices.
For additional details on the MSCI ESG Ratings Model, refer to Section 2, Data, ratings and scores, of
“ESG Ratings Methodology.”

Risks associated with this Key Issue
• Damage to brand value from loss of consumer trust or negative publicity.
• Increased costs to comply with additional regulatory requirements or litigation.
• Increased costs of implementing large-scale product recalls or to fulfill warranties.
Product Safety & Quality Key Issue score
The Product Safety & Quality Key Issue score evaluates the company’s level of exposure to, and
management of, risks on this Key Issue. The Key Issue score is based on the Exposure score and the
Management score using the formula below. The Exposure score and the Management score are
combined such that a higher level of exposure requires a higher level of demonstrated management
capability in order to achieve the same overall Key Issue score.
𝐾𝐼 = 7 − (max⁡(𝐸𝑋𝑃 ,2) − 𝑀𝐺𝑀𝑇 )
Where:
• 𝐾𝐼 is the Key Issue score for company 𝑖.
• 𝐸𝑋𝑃 is the Exposure score for company 𝑖.
• 𝑀𝐺𝑀𝑇 ⁡is the Management score for company 𝑖.

Product Safety & Quality Management score
The Product Safety & Quality Management score evaluates the company’s ability to manage its exposure
to risks on this Key Issue. It is based on weighted average of the score associated with each relevant
indicator, modified by controversies.

This score is derived from indicators that are scored on a 0-10 scale, with 10 corresponding to best
practice, and 0 corresponding to lack of management. Refer to Section 3.3, Analyzing risk management,
of “ESG Ratings Methodology” for additional details. Sources are company disclosures except where
otherwise indicated.

The definitions of the data points in each component are given below:
Product Safety & Quality Practices score
Assesses the company’s ability to manage its exposure to risks related to the strength of its supply chain
and sourcing systems, its quality management efforts in manufacturing and its responsible marketing
practices. This score is a component of the Product Safety & Quality Management score (excluding
controversies) and considers attributes of the company's policies and initiatives. Expressed as a 0–10
score, where 10 indicates strong initiatives.
• Existence of contingency plans/mitigation control systems to ensure that products are in
stock, reliable and safe
Definition: Indicates whether the company has contingency plans/mitigation control systems to ensure
that products are in stock, reliable, and safe.
• Measures and reports quantitative indicators related to service quality performance or
customer protection
Definition: Indicates whether the company measures and reports quantitative indicators related to
service quality performance or customer protection (e.g., clinical quality reports, customer surveys).
• Certification to product safety or quality standard
Definition: Indicates whether the company's products are certified to internationally recognized safety
and quality standards. Expressed as a 0-10 score, with 10 indicating strong initiatives.
o Extent of certification to a widely accepted product safety/quality standard
Definition: Indicates whether the company certifies its own operations with a widely accepted
product safety/quality standard (e.g., HACCP, ISO 9001, ISO/TS 16949, ISO 13485 or equivalent).
o Extent of certification to an internally developed product safety/quality standard
Definition: Indicates whether the company certifies its own operations with an internally
developed product safety/quality standard.
• Scope of employee training on product quality
Definition: The scope of the company’s employee training on product safety and quality. Best practice is
for all employees to receive training on product quality standards.

• Extent of product testing capacity
Definition: The extent of the company’s product testing capacity, e.g., third-party or in-house testing.
• Audit/control procedures on responsible marketing
Definition: Indicates whether the company conducts audits or control procedures to assess compliance
with its responsible marketing policies.
• Policy on responsible marketing, advertising and sales
Definition: Indicates whether the company has explicitly stated a policy on responsible marketing,
advertising and sales.
• Membership in recognized industry-wide partnership(s) on supply chain risk evaluation and
mitigation
Definition: Indicates whether the company is a member of industry initiatives or partnerships that
evaluate supply chain risk and undertake relevant mitigation programs.
• Supplier certification level
Definition: Assesses whether suppliers at each level (e.g., Tier 1, Tier 2, Tier 3) possess relevant safety,
and quality certifications. Expressed as a 0-10 score, with 10 indicating strong initiatives.
o General statement on supplier certification of quality procedures
Definition: Indicates whether the company makes general statements regarding the certification
or oversight of its supply chain quality, without providing further detail on certification at specific
levels of its supply chain
o Tier 1 - Direct supplier facilities and processes certified by company employees or
third-party auditors
Definition: Indicates whether the company oversees the quality processes of its direct supplier
(Tier 1) facilities and processes through certification or audits by a third party or by company
employees.
o Tier 2 - Indirect/sub supplier facilities and processes certified by company
employees or third-party auditors

Definition: Indicates whether the company oversees the quality processes of its indirect/sub-
supplier (Tier 2) facilities and processes through certification or audits by a third party or by
company employees.
o Tier 3 - Ingredients/raw materials checked for quality on a regular basis
Definition: Indicates whether the company oversees the quality processes of its ingredients/raw
materials (Tier 3) through certification or audits by a third party or by company employees.
• Scope of supplier training on quality standards
Definition: The extent to which the company trains suppliers on quality standards, requirements, and
processes. Best practice is to train all suppliers.
• Product responsibility & integrity
Definition: Assesses how responsibly and ethically a company designs, delivers and promotes its
products and services. Expressed as a 0-10 score, with 10 indicating strong initiatives.
o Medical Loss Ratio (MLR) performance score
Definition: Assesses the company’s Medical Loss Ratio, reflecting the proportion of premiums
spent on medical services versus administrative costs. Higher scores indicate stronger alignment
with service quality and regulatory expectations in managed healthcare. Applicable to Managed
Healthcare industry only.
o Teaching staff score
Definition: Assesses the proportion of teaching staff relative to the total workforce. Applicable to
Education Services industry only.
o Instruction to marketing expense ratio score
Definition: Assesses the proportion of instruction and student services expenses to marketing
and recruitment expenses. Applicable to Education Services industry only.
o Marketing and recruitment expenses score
Definition: Assesses the proportion of marketing expenses relative to the total sales revenue.
Applicable to Education Services industry only.

o Responsible gambling policy & practices score
Definition: Assesses the company's implementation of responsible gambling standards, policies,
and player protection measures. Applicable to Casinos & Gaming industry only.
o Antibiotics use policy score
Definition: Assesses the company's policy framework and certifications related to antibiotic use
in meat production and aquaculture. Applicable to Restaurants industry only.
o Antibiotics phaseout targets
Definition: Assesses the presence and robustness of issuer plans to phase out non-therapeutic
or high-risk antibiotic use in meat production and aquaculture . Applicable to Restaurants
industry only.
Product Safety & Quality Performance score
Assesses the company's performance on product safety & quality metrics (including recalls, regulatory
warnings and/or warranty payments along with other industry specific metrics if applicable). Expressed
as a 0–10 score, where 10 indicates strong performance.
• Regulatory warning performance relative to peers
Definition: Assesses the company’s performance based on number or regulatory warnings (warning
letters and U.S. FDA form 483s (“Form 483”)) and their intensities (normalized by sales) issued by
regulatory authorities, relative to peers. Expressed as a 0–10 score, where 10 indicates strong
performance.
o Industry relative warning letters performance score
Definition: Assesses the company’s performance on three-year average of total number of
Warning Letters received (both absolute and sales normalized), relative to its peers. Expressed as
a 0–10 score, where 10 indicates strong performance.
o Three-year average warning letters received (absolute)
Definition: Measures the company’s three-year average number of warning letters
received.
o Three-year average warning letters received (sales normalized)

Definition: Measures the company’s three year average number of warning letters received,
normalized by sales.
o Industry relative Form 483 performance score
Definition: Assesses the company’s performance on three-year average of total number of Form
483s received (both absolute and sales normalized), relative to its peers. Expressed as a 0–10
score, where 10 indicates strong performance.
o Three-year average Form 483 received (absolute)
Definition: Measures the company’s three-year average of absolute number of Form
483s received.
o Three-year average Form 483 received (sales normalized)
Definition: Measures the company’s three year average number of Form 483 received,
normalized by sales.
• Warranty performance relative to peers
Definition: Assesses the company's performance on warranty payments (normalized by sales) and its
trend, relative to industry peers. Expressed as a 0-10 score, where 10 indicates
o Warranty payments industry relative score
Definition: Assesses the company’s warranty payments intensity (per unit of sales or),
relative to industry peers. Expressed as a 0–10 score, where 10 indicates strong performance.
o Three-year average warranty payments (per million revenue)
Definition: Measures the company’s three-year average warranty payments
normalized by revenue.
o Warranty Payments Industry Relative Trend score
Definition: Assesses the company’s performance on the three-year average of year-over-
year warranty payments intensity trend (per unit of sales), relative to industry peers.
Expressed as a 0–10 score, where 10 indicates strong performance.
o Three-year average year-over-year warranty payments trend (per million
revenue)
Definition: Measures the company’s three-year average of year-over-year change in
warranty payments normalized by revenue.

• Product recall performance relative to peers
Definition: Assesses the company's performance with respect to product recalls, relative to industry
peers. Expressed as a 0–10 score, where 10 indicates strong performance.
o Industry relative recalls performance score (absolute)
Definition: Assesses the company’s performance on the total number of recalls,
disaggregated by severity (severe, moderate, and minor), relative to industry peers.
Expressed as a 0–10 score, where 10 indicates strong performance.
▪ Three-year average absolute total severe recalls
Definition: Measures the company’s three-year average of absolute total
number of recalls that are severe in nature.
▪ Three-year average absolute total moderate recalls
Definition: Measures the company’s three-year average of absolute total
number of recalls that are moderate in nature.
▪ Three-year average absolute total minor recalls
Definition: Measures the company’s three-year average of absolute total
number of recalls that are minor in nature.
o Industry relative recalls performance score (sales based)
Definition: Assesses the company’s performance on recall intensity normalized by sales,
disaggregated by severity (severe, moderate, and minor), relative to industry peers.
Expressed as a 0–10 score, where 10 indicates strong performance.
▪ Three-year average total severe recalls (sales based)
Definition: Measures the company’s three-year average of total number of
recalls that are moderate in nature normalized by sales.
▪ Three-year average total moderate recalls (sales based)
Definition: Measures the company’s three-year average of total number of
recalls that are moderate in nature normalized by sales.
▪ Three-year average total minor recalls (sales based)
Definition: Measures the company’s three-year average of total number of
recalls that are minor in nature normalized by sales.

o Automobile recalls performance score
Definition: Assesses the company’s overall performance on recall intensity and trend metrics
(vehicles recalled per vehicle manufactured or sold) relative to its peers. Expressed as a 0–10
score, where 10 indicates the highest level of performance. Applicable to automobiles industry
only.
o Recalls per vehicle sales industry relative score
Definition: Assesses the company’s performance on vehicle-recall intensity metrics
(vehicles recalled per vehicle sold), relative to its peers. Expressed as a 0–10 score,
where 10 indicates the highest level of performance.
▪ Three-year average of recalls (normalized by number of vehicles sold)
Definition: Measures the company’s three-year average of total number of
recalls, normalized by number of vehicles sold.
o Recalls per vehicle sales industry relative trend score
Definition: Assesses the company’s performance on the three-year average year-
over-year trend in vehicle-recall intensity (vehicles recalled per vehicle sold), relative
to its peers. Expressed as a 0–10 score, where 10 indicates the highest level of
performance.
▪ Three-year average of year-over-year trend in recalls (normalized by
number of vehicles sold)
Definition: Measures the company’s three-year average of year-over-trend in
total number of recalls, normalized by number of vehicles sold.
• Industry-specific Product Safety and Quality Performance score
Definition: Assesses the company's performance on industry-specific metrics related to product
safety and quality. Expressed as a 0-10 score, where 10 indicates the highest level of performance.
o Airworthiness directives performance score
Definition: Assesses the company’s performance on compliance with airworthiness directives
issued by aviation regulators over a three-year period relative to its peers. Expressed as a 0–10
score, where 10 indicates the highest level of performance. Applicable to Aerospace & Defense
companies with revenues in Aircrafts segments only.
o Industry Relative airworthiness directives intensity score

Definition: Assesses the company’s performance on airworthiness-directive intensity
metrics (number of airworthiness directives per sales) relative to its peers. Expressed
as a 0–10 score, where 10 indicates strong performance.
▪ Three-year average airworthiness directives intensity
Definition: Measures the company’s three-year average number of airworthiness
directives normalized by sales.
o Air incidents performance score
Definition: Assesses the company’s performance on aviation incidents leading to fatalities and damage
caused to the aircraft due to aviation incidents. Expressed as a 0–10 score, where 10 indicates the
highest level of performance. Applicable to Passenger airlines industry only.
o Aviation Incidents Fatality score
Definition: Assesses the company’s performance on number of fatalities due to air
incidents. Expressed as a 0–10 score, where 10 indicates the highest level of
performance.
▪ Three-year average number of fatalities
Definition: Measures the company’s three year average number of fatalities
caused due to aviation incidents.
o Industry Relative Aircraft Damage intensity score
Definition: Assesses the company’s performance on damage caused to the aircraft
intensity (normalized by sales), relative to peers. Expressed as a 0–10 score, where 10
indicates the highest level of performance.
▪ Three-year average aircraft damage intensity
Definition: Measures the company’s three-year average of aircrafts damaged
intensity (normalized by sales) due to aviation incidents.
o Managed healthcare performance score
Definition: Assesses the company’s performance on healthcare plan quality and safety metrics based on
CMS Star Ratings or IDSS scores. Expressed as a 0–10 score, where 10 indicates the highest level of
performance. Applicable to managed healthcare industry only.
o Water quality standards score

Definition: Assesses the company’s performance on compliance with drinking-water-quality
standards and regulations. Expressed as a 0–10 score, where 10 indicates strong performance.
Applicable to water utilities industry only.
o Labelling or marketing incidents performance score
Definition: Assesses the company’s performance on compliance with industry or regulatory
labeling and marketing codes. Expressed as a 0–10 score, where 10 indicates strong
performance. Applicable to Beverages industry only.
Controversies
A controversy deduction ranging from 0 to 5 points is subtracted from the overall Management score
based on the severity, status, and the company’s role in the controversies facing the company on this
Key Issue. The following categories of controversies are used in the assessment:
• Product safety and quality controversies.
• Customer fraud and billing controversies.
• False marketing controversies.
For more details on how controversies are included in the MSCI ESG Ratings model, refer to Section
3.3.2, Controversies cases, of “ESG Ratings Methodology.”
Product Safety & Quality Exposure score
The Product Safety & Quality Exposure score evaluates the company’s exposure to risks on this Key
Issue. It is based on the Business Exposure score only. The Business Exposure score is scored on a 0-10
scale, with 10 corresponding to the highest risk and 0 corresponding to the lowest risk. Refer to Section
3.2, Analyzing risk exposure, of “ESG Ratings Methodology” for additional details. The following formula
is used in the Exposure score calculation:
𝐸𝑋𝑃 = 𝐵𝑈𝑆
Where:
• 𝐸𝑋𝑃 is the Product Safety & Quality Exposure score of company 𝑖.
• 𝐵𝑈𝑆 is the Business Exposure score of company 𝑖.

Business Exposure score
The Business Exposure score is a weighted average of the Business Segment Exposure scores of a
company’s business segments. Scores are weighted by the proportion of a company’s total revenue in
each business segment, using the following formula to calculate the Business Exposure score:
𝐵𝑈𝑆 =⁡∑ 𝑤 𝐵𝑆𝐸
Where:
• 𝐵𝑆𝐸 is the Business Segment Exposure score for business segment 𝑗.
• 𝑤 is the weight of business segment 𝑗 for company 𝑖 based on the contribution to total
company revenue.
• 𝑛 is the number of business segments of company 𝑖.
Business Segment Exposure score
The Business Segment Exposure score of a business segment is based on a mapping of business
segments as disclosed by the company to a corresponding business activity. MSCI S&C uses the
Standard Industrial Classification (SIC) system along with industry-specific adjustments to define
business activities. The score associated with a business activity is used to calculate a Business

Segment Exposure score. Each business activity score is calculated as the maximum of the Warranty
and Recalls score, Marketing and Services score, Retail score, Content Integrity score and Safety score
of a business activity:
𝐵𝑆𝐸 = max⁡(𝑊&𝑅 ,⁡𝑀&𝑆 ,⁡𝐶𝐼𝑆 ,⁡𝑆𝑆 )
Where:
• 𝑊&𝑅 is the Warranty and Recalls score for business activity 𝑗.
• ⁡𝑀&𝑆 is the Marketing and Services score for business activity 𝑗.
• ⁡𝐶𝐼𝑆 is the Content Integrity score for business activity 𝑗.
• ⁡𝑆𝑆 is the Safety score for business activity 𝑗.
The Warranty and Recalls score is calculated as the average of the Warranty score, Safety Regulator
score and Recalls score. The Warranty score is calculated from the average warranty reserve ratio
(warranty reserves/total assets). The Safety Regulator score is developed from a qualitative assessment
of whether a business activity is regulated in the United States by the FDA, the National Highway Traffic
Safety Administration (NHTSA) or Federal Aviation Administration. The Recalls score is calculated from
the number of recalls for each business activity.
The Marketing and Services score is a qualitative assessment depending on (1) whether the business
activity is regulated in the United States by the Federal Trade Commission’s (FTC’s) bureau for
marketing and advertising regulations and (2) whether the business activity provides services or
products that have addictive properties.
The Content Integrity score is a qualitative assessment of the integrity of the information provided by
business activities and is specific to media outlets.
The Safety score is calculated from annual death rates attributable to select business activities that carry
health risks (e.g., through injury, contamination or intoxication).
